Happy for you to use `// NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-reinterpret-cast)` to address these for now.

Thanks. I added these. 

Now it's failing with 

```
src/compiler.h:8:0: error: #error The libpldm implementation requires __has_attribute
``` 

Is this expected?

From the most recent CI run above the problem is:

> You must document your changes under include/libpldm in CHANGELOG.md

As for

> src/compiler.h:8:0: error: #error The libpldm implementation requires __has_attribute

I really wish we'd just turn off `cppcheck`, it's incredibly noisy and everyone ignores it
Thanks for pointing this out.
Hi Kasun, thanks for the patch! I have a few comments inline.
Hi Andrew, thanks for helping to review these patches. I made the changes. Please take a look again.
Can you split this comment out to a separate patch? Essentially it's a fix for the change that introduced it.
Created a separate commit: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/83536

These are already provided in `include/libpldm/entity.h`:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/include/libpldm/entity.h#L23-L24
Removed
Do we need to expose this?
I am just using this to verify the pdr_data->file_name.length and pdr_data->oem_file_classification_name.length is within limits. So I guess we do not need to expose this. Moved to platform.c file

APIs throughout the library typically use the opposite order for these parameters. Can you please switch them around such that the length follows the pointer?

Also, can you please:

1. Make `resp_pdr_buffer` type `void *`
2. Take `buffer_len` as a type `size_t *`, and [as an in-out parameter](https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L270-L272)

As for some nits, I'd prefer we called `pdr_data` just `pdr`, and `resp_pdr_buffer` just `buf` or `buffer`, or better yet, `data` and `data_len` to match `decode_pldm_platform_file_descriptor_pdr()` below.
Done
This should be `0`, not `1` (or change `>` to `>=`).
The name should include the length of the NULL character. So a valid name should be at least 2 bytes
If this is where the value is used, can we move its definition here into the implementation, instead of exposing it in the library API?
Done
See related comment above.
The name should include the length of the NULL character. So a valid name should be at least 2 bytes
With respect to the comment about an in-out parameter for the buffer length on the header, you need to use `pldm_msgbuf_complete_used()` here so the encoded length is provided back to the caller.
Done
Nice one!
